newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares dive amid worries on new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares dive amid worries on new govt.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Tuesday morning amid fresh doubts about the formation of a Islamist-free coalition, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 stood at 1,718 at 0851 GMT in late morning trade, down 3.16 percent, or 56 points from Monday when it surged 8.04 percent on hopes of a secularist alliance.

"The market was irritated by the possibility that conservative True Path Party may not support the new alliance. (Leftist leader Deniz) Baykal's remarks also had a negative effect. Sales may continue," said Okan Gulek from Taksim securities.
Some brokers said profit-taking after Monday's steep rise also played a role in the fall.

Baykal told a meeting of his Republican People's Party deputies that they were in favour of giving a vote of confidence to the new coalition planned by conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, but he wanted to see any alliance to be headed by Yilmaz going to early elections by the end of 1997.
Yilmaz, nominated last week to replace Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, has said he wants to take the country to the polls next spring.
Conservative rival Tansu Ciller's True Path Party late on Monday rebuffed an invitation by Yilmaz to join his planned coalition. Yilmaz and Ciller are nevertheless due to meet later today.
Yilmaz is short of the simple majority needed in parliament to win a confidence vote even with the support of two left-wing parties and a tiny right-wing grouping which broke away from the DYP.
